sections.section_name: Section A (Comprehension & Knowledge)
sections.instructions: Read the unseen passage/case study and answer the factual, MCQ, and inferential queries (1 Mark each).

questions.question_text: [Case Study Passage Set 1] Read the travel log: 'Raman's family drove from Delhi to Jaipur. Odometer reading at start was 42,150 km and at destination was 42,430 km.' What is the place value of digit 4 in the initial reading 42,150 km?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Step 1: Digit 4 is in the Ten Thousands (TTh) column. Step 2: Value = 4 x 10,000 = 40,000. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: What is the net distance traveled by Raman's family in the passage above?
questions.correct_answer: 280 km
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Distance Delta = Final Reading - Start Reading = 42,430 - 42,150 = 280 km. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: When 42,430 is rounded off to the nearest hundred, the resulting estimated distance is:
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Tens digit is 3 (< 5), so 42,430 rounds down to 42,400. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Which digit permutation of 4, 2, 1, 5, 0 forms the greatest possible 5-digit number?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Arrange digits in descending order: 5, 4, 2, 1, 0 -> 54,210. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: What is the predecessor of 42,150?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Predecessor = Number - 1 = 42,150 - 1 = 42,149. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section B (Textual / Core Subject Application)
sections.instructions: Answer the core subject short-answer problem statements based on NCERT concepts (3 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Express the 5-digit number 67,543 in expanded notation and state the place value and face value of digit 7.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Expanded form = 60,000 + 7,000 + 500 + 40 + 3. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Place value of 7 = 7 x 1,000 = 7,000. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Face value of 7 = 7 (the digit itself). (1 Mark)
Total: 3 Marks.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following 5-digit travel distances in ascending order: 58,042 km; 58,402 km; 58,024 km; 58,240 km.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Compare Ten Thousands and Thousands digits (all 58). (1 Mark)
Step 2: Compare Hundreds digits: 58,024 (H=0, T=2), 58,042 (H=0, T=4), 58,240 (H=2), 58,402 (H=4). (1 Mark)
Step 3: Ascending order: 58,024 km < 58,042 km < 58,240 km < 58,402 km. (1 Mark)
Total: 3 Marks.

questions.question_text: A vehicle's odometer reads 24,850 km. Round this reading off to: (a) Nearest 10, (b) Nearest 100, (c) Nearest 1,000.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Nearest 10: Ones digit is 0 -> 24,850. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Nearest 100: Tens digit is 5 -> Rounds up to 24,900. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Nearest 1,000: Hundreds digit is 8 (>=5) -> Rounds up to 25,000. (1 Mark)
Total: 3 Marks.

sections.section_name: Section C (Grammar / Skill Items / Analytical Exercises)
sections.instructions: Solve the procedural skill drills, rule application problems, and equation conversions (4 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Form the greatest and smallest 5-digit numbers using the digits 8, 0, 5, 3, 2 without repetition. Calculate their difference.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Arrange digits in descending order for Greatest Number = 85,320. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Arrange digits in ascending order for Smallest Number (ensuring 0 is not leading digit) = 20,358. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Column Subtraction setup: 85,320 - 20,358. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Result: 85,320 - 20,358 = 64,962. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: A motor boat travels at a speed of 20 km/h. (a) How far will it travel in 3.5 hours? (b) How long will it take to cover 100 km?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Formula Distance = Speed x Time. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Part (a) Distance = 20 x 3.5 = 70 km. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Formula Time = Distance / Speed. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Part (b) Time = 100 / 20 = 5 hours. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: Rule Application Drill: Apply rounding rules to estimate the total sum of 34,820 km + 25,190 km by rounding each number to the nearest thousand first. Compare with actual sum.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Round 34,820 to nearest thousand = 35,000. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Round 25,190 to nearest thousand = 25,000. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Estimated Sum = 35,000 + 25,000 = 60,000. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Actual Sum = 34,820 + 25,190 = 60,010. Difference = 10 km. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

sections.section_name: Section D (Creative / Long Answer / Synthesizing Questions)
sections.instructions: Complete the guided paragraph prompts, diagrammatic descriptions, and multi-step analytical tasks (6 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Case Study & Multi-step Task: Gracy took a bank loan of ₹4,000 to buy a fishing net. She paid back ₹345 every month for 1 year (12 months). (a) Calculate total amount paid in 12 months. (b) Calculate total interest paid. (c) If she saved ₹500 every month from fish sales, what was her net annual profit after paying the monthly loan installment?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Part (a) Total loan payment = 345 x 12 = ₹4,140. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Part (b) Total Interest = Total Paid - Loan Principal = 4,140 - 4,000 = ₹140. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Part (c) Total annual savings = 500 x 12 = ₹6,000. Net Profit after loan = 6,000 - 4,140 = ₹1,860. (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Guided Paragraph & Travel Logistics Synthesis: Write a structured report analyzing a 3-day road trip. Day 1: 345 km, Day 2: 412 km, Day 3: 288 km. Vehicle fuel efficiency is 15 km per litre, and diesel costs ₹90 per litre. Compute: (1) Total trip distance, (2) Total fuel needed, (3) Total fuel cost.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Total Distance = 345 + 412 + 288 = 1,045 km. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Fuel Needed = Total Distance / Efficiency = 1,045 / 15 = 69.67 litres. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Total Fuel Cost = 69.67 x 90 = ₹6,270.30. (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Diagrammatic Description & Odometer Tracking: Describe an odometer display diagram transitioning from 78,995 km to 79,030 km during a delivery run. Compute distance covered, round distance to nearest ten, and calculate average vehicle speed if trip took 30 minutes (0.5 hours).
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Odometer Delta = 79,030 - 78,995 = 35 km. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Round 35 km to nearest ten -> 40 km. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Average Speed = Distance / Time = 35 / 0.5 = 70 km/h. (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Creative Synthesis & Budgeting Prompt: A fisherwomen cooperative (Vankar Bank) has 20 members. Each member saves ₹25 every month. (a) Total monthly savings of cooperative? (b) Total savings in 2 years? (c) If they buy a mini-truck costing ₹12,000 using bank savings, how much balance remains?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Monthly Savings = 20 members x ₹25 = ₹500/month. (2 Marks)
Step 2: 2 Years = 24 months. Total Savings = 500 x 24 = ₹12,000. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Remaining Balance = 12,000 - 12,000 = ₹0 balance remaining. (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

question_papers.theme: Equal Sharing, Same Whole Rule, Fraction Kits & Mixed Numbers

sections.section_name: Section A (Comprehension & Knowledge)
sections.instructions: Read the unseen passage/case study and answer the factual, MCQ, and inferential queries (1 Mark each).

questions.question_text: [Case Study Passage Set 1] Read the scenario: 'Sheela and Raman bought 3 equal-sized parathas and shared them equally among 4 children.' What fraction of a whole paratha does each child receive?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total items = 3, Total recipients = 4. Each share = 3/4 of a paratha. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: In the fraction 3/4, what does the denominator 4 represent?
options: Total equal parts in one whole
Number of children who didn't eat
questions.correct_answer: Total equal parts in one whole
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Denominator (bottom number) defines the total equal divisions of one whole unit. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: (3x2)/(4x2) = 6/8. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: According to the 'Same Whole Rule', can 1/2 of a small paratha be compared directly with 1/2 of a large jumbo paratha?
options: No, because the wholes are not identical in size
Yes, because 1/2 is always equal to 1/2
questions.correct_answer: No, because the wholes are not identical in size
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Same Whole Rule: Fractional parts can only be compared if derived from identical whole units. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Express the improper fraction 7/4 as a mixed number.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 7 / 4 = 1 with remainder 3 -> 1 3/4. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section B (Textual / Core Subject Application)
sections.instructions: Answer the core subject short-answer problem statements based on NCERT concepts (3 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Using a fraction strip model, demonstrate why 2/4 is equivalent to 1/2 and 4/8.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Draw 1 unit strip divided into 2 equal parts; 1 part = 1/2. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Divide identical unit strip into 4 parts; 2 parts = 2/4, covering exact same length as 1/2. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Divide unit strip into 8 parts; 4 parts = 4/8, covering exact same length. Thus 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8. (1 Mark)
Total: 3 Marks.

questions.question_text: Raman ate 2/7 of a cake on Monday and 3/7 on Tuesday. What fraction of the cake did he eat in total, and what fraction remains?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Total eaten = 2/7 + 3/7 = (2+3)/7 = 5/7 of the cake. (1.5 Marks)
Step 2: Remaining fraction = Whole - Eaten = 7/7 - 5/7 = 2/7 of the cake. (1.5 Marks)
Total: 3 Marks.

questions.question_text: Convert the improper fraction 11/3 into a mixed number, and convert the mixed number 2 3/5 into an improper fraction.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: 11 / 3 = 3 Quotient, 2 Remainder -> 11/3 = 3 2/3. (1.5 Marks)
Step 2: 2 3/5 = (2 x 5 + 3) / 5 = (10 + 3) / 5 = 13/5. (1.5 Marks)
Total: 3 Marks.

sections.section_name: Section C (Grammar / Skill Items / Analytical Exercises)
sections.instructions: Solve the procedural skill drills, rule application problems, and equation conversions (4 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Find three equivalent fractions for 2/5 by multiplying, and simplify the fraction 18/24 to its lowest terms by dividing.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Equivalent 1 = (2x2)/(5x2) = 4/10. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Equivalent 2 = (2x3)/(5x3) = 6/15; Equivalent 3 = (2x4)/(5x4) = 8/20. (1 Mark)
Step 3: HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. Divide numerator and denominator by 6. (1 Mark)
Step 4: 18/6 = 3, 24/6 = 4 -> Simplified fraction = 3/4. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: Compare the following fraction pairs using '>', '<', or '=' and show working: (a) 3/8 vs 5/8, (b) 2/3 vs 3/5.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Part (a) Same denominators (8): Compare numerators 3 < 5 -> 3/8 < 5/8. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Part (b) Different denominators (3 and 5): Find Common Denominator = 15. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Convert 2/3 = 10/15 and 3/5 = 9/15. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Compare 10/15 > 9/15 -> 2/3 > 3/5. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: A basket contains 36 fruits. 1/3 are apples, 1/4 are oranges, and the rest are bananas. Calculate the exact count of each fruit.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Apples = 1/3 of 36 = 36 / 3 = 12 apples. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Oranges = 1/4 of 36 = 36 / 4 = 9 oranges. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Total apples and oranges = 12 + 9 = 21 fruits. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Bananas = 36 - 21 = 15 bananas. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

sections.section_name: Section D (Creative / Long Answer / Synthesizing Questions)
sections.instructions: Complete the guided paragraph prompts, diagrammatic descriptions, and multi-step analytical tasks (6 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Case Study & Multi-step Task: Fresh fish costs ₹150 per kg. When dried, it shrinks to 1/3 of its original fresh weight. Dried fish sells at ₹450 per kg. (a) How much dried fish is obtained from 60 kg fresh fish? (b) Calculate total cost of 60 kg fresh fish. (c) Calculate total earning from selling the dried fish and net profit.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Part (a) Dried weight = 1/3 of 60 kg = 20 kg. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Part (b) Fresh fish cost = 60 kg x ₹150 = ₹9,000. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Part (c) Dried fish sale = 20 kg x ₹450 = ₹9,000. Net profit = ₹9,000 - ₹9,000 = ₹0 (Break-even). (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Guided Visual & Fraction Strip Synthesis: Construct a detailed visual fraction wall diagram comparing 1 Whole, 1/2s, 1/4s, and 1/8s. Answer: (1) How many 1/8 strips equal 3/4? (2) Is 2/4 + 2/8 equal to 3/4? Show step-by-step fractional calculation.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Draw fraction wall diagram showing 1 = 2x(1/2) = 4x(1/4) = 8x(1/8). (2 Marks)
Step 2: Part (1) 3/4 = (3x2)/8 = 6/8 -> Six 1/8 strips equal 3/4. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Part (2) 2/4 = 4/8, so 2/4 + 2/8 = 4/8 + 2/8 = 6/8 = 3/4. Yes, statement is TRUE! (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Creative Recipe Scaling Task: A cake recipe for 4 people requires 1/2 kg flour, 1/4 kg sugar, 1/8 kg butter, and 1/4 L milk. Scale this recipe for 12 people (3 times original yield). Calculate required quantities of each ingredient in grams/millilitres.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Scaling factor = 12 / 4 = 3 times. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Flour = 3 x (1/2 kg) = 3/2 kg = 1.5 kg = 1,500 g. (1.5 Marks)
Step 3: Sugar = 3 x (1/4 kg) = 3/4 kg = 750 g; Butter = 3 x (1/8 kg) = 3/8 kg = 375 g. (2 Marks)
Step 4: Milk = 3 x (1/4 L) = 3/4 L = 750 ml. (1.5 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Multi-part Fraction Word Problem: A school library has 120 books. 2/5 are Mathematics, 1/3 are Science, 1/6 are Storybooks, and the rest are Art books. Calculate: (a) Number of Math and Science books, (b) Number of Art books, (c) Fraction of total books that are Art books.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Math = 2/5 x 120 = 48; Science = 1/3 x 120 = 40. Total = 88 books. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Storybooks = 1/6 x 120 = 20 books. Total Math+Sci+Story = 88 + 20 = 108 books. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Art books = 120 - 108 = 12 books. Fraction Art books = 12 / 120 = 1/10. (2 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

Step 1: Scaling factor = 12 / 4 = 3 times. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Flour = 3 x (1/2 kg) = 3/2 kg = 1.5 kg = 1,500 g. (1.5 Marks)
Step 3: Sugar = 3 x (1/4 kg) = 3/4 kg = 750 g; Butter = 3 x (1/8 kg) = 3/8 kg = 375 g. (2 Marks)
Step 4: Milk = 3 x (1/4 L) = 3/4 L = 750 ml. (1.5 Marks)
Total: 6 Marks.

questions.question_text: Multi-part Fraction Word Problem: A school library has 120 books. 2/5 are Mathematics, 1/3 are Science, 1/6 are Storybooks, and the rest are Art books. Calculate: (a) Number of Math and Science books, (b) Number of Art books, (c) Fraction of total books that are Art books.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Math = 2/5 x 120 = 48; Science = 1/3 x 120 = 40. Total = 88 books. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Storybooks = 1/6 x 120 = 20 books. Total Math+Sci+Story = 88 + 20 = 108 books. (2 Marks)

Total: 6 Marks.

sections.section_name: Section A (Comprehension & Knowledge)

questions.question_text: [Case Study Passage Set 3] Read the scenario: 'Sheela and Raman bought 3 equal-sized parathas and shared them equally among 4 children.' What fraction of a whole paratha does each child receive?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Total items = 3, Total recipients = 4. Each share = 3/4 of a paratha. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: In the fraction 3/4, what does the denominator 4 represent?
options: Total equal parts in one whole
Number of children who didn't eat
questions.correct_answer: Total equal parts in one whole
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Denominator (bottom number) defines the total equal divisions of one whole unit. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: (3x2)/(4x2) = 6/8. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: According to the 'Same Whole Rule', can 1/2 of a small paratha be compared directly with 1/2 of a large jumbo paratha?
options: No, because the wholes are not identical in size
Yes, because 1/2 is always equal to 1/2
questions.correct_answer: No, because the wholes are not identical in size
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Same Whole Rule: Fractional parts can only be compared if derived from identical whole units. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Express the improper fraction 7/4 as a mixed number.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 7 / 4 = 1 with remainder 3 -> 1 3/4. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section B (Textual / Core Subject Application)
sections.instructions: Answer the core subject short-answer problem statements based on NCERT concepts (3 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Using a fraction strip model, demonstrate why 2/4 is equivalent to 1/2 and 4/8.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Draw 1 unit strip divided into 2 equal parts; 1 part = 1/2. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Divide identical unit strip into 4 parts; 2 parts = 2/4, covering exact same length as 1/2. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Divide unit strip into 8 parts; 4 parts = 4/8, covering exact same length. Thus 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8. (1 Mark)
Total: 3 Marks.

questions.question_text: Raman ate 2/7 of a cake on Monday and 3/7 on Tuesday. What fraction of the cake did he eat in total, and what fraction remains?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Total eaten = 2/7 + 3/7 = (2+3)/7 = 5/7 of the cake. (1.5 Marks)
Step 2: Remaining fraction = Whole - Eaten = 7/7 - 5/7 = 2/7 of the cake. (1.5 Marks)
Total: 3 Marks.

questions.question_text: Convert the improper fraction 11/3 into a mixed number, and convert the mixed number 2 3/5 into an improper fraction.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: 11 / 3 = 3 Quotient, 2 Remainder -> 11/3 = 3 2/3. (1.5 Marks)
Step 2: 2 3/5 = (2 x 5 + 3) / 5 = (10 + 3) / 5 = 13/5. (1.5 Marks)
Total: 3 Marks.

sections.section_name: Section C (Grammar / Skill Items / Analytical Exercises)
sections.instructions: Solve the procedural skill drills, rule application problems, and equation conversions (4 Marks each).

questions.question_text: Find three equivalent fractions for 2/5 by multiplying, and simplify the fraction 18/24 to its lowest terms by dividing.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Equivalent 1 = (2x2)/(5x2) = 4/10. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Equivalent 2 = (2x3)/(5x3) = 6/15; Equivalent 3 = (2x4)/(5x4) = 8/20. (1 Mark)
Step 3: HCF of 18 and 24 is 6. Divide numerator and denominator by 6. (1 Mark)
Step 4: 18/6 = 3, 24/6 = 4 -> Simplified fraction = 3/4. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: Compare the following fraction pairs using '>', '<', or '=' and show working: (a) 3/8 vs 5/8, (b) 2/3 vs 3/5.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Part (a) Same denominators (8): Compare numerators 3 < 5 -> 3/8 < 5/8. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Part (b) Different denominators (3 and 5): Find Common Denominator = 15. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Convert 2/3 = 10/15 and 3/5 = 9/15. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Compare 10/15 > 9/15 -> 2/3 > 3/5. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: A basket contains 36 fruits. 1/3 are apples, 1/4 are oranges, and the rest are bananas. Calculate the exact count of each fruit.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Apples = 1/3 of 36 = 36 / 3 = 12 apples. (1 Mark)
Step 2: Oranges = 1/4 of 36 = 36 / 4 = 9 oranges. (1 Mark)
Step 3: Total apples and oranges = 12 + 9 = 21 fruits. (1 Mark)
Step 4: Bananas = 36 - 21 = 15 bananas. (1 Mark)
Total: 4 Marks.

questions.question_text: Case Study & Multi-step Task: Fresh fish costs ₹150 per kg. When dried, it shrinks to 1/3 of its original fresh weight. Dried fish sells at ₹450 per kg. (a) How much dried fish is obtained from 60 kg fresh fish? (b) Calculate total cost of 60 kg fresh fish. (c) Calculate total earning from selling the dried fish and net profit.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Step 1: Part (a) Dried weight = 1/3 of 60 kg = 20 kg. (2 Marks)
Step 2: Part (b) Fresh fish cost = 60 kg x ₹150 = ₹9,000. (2 Marks)
Step 3: Part (c) Dried fish sale = 20 kg x ₹450 = ₹9,000. Net profit = ₹9,000 - ₹9,000 = ₹0 (Break-even). (2 Marks)

ch01.title: 5-Digit Place Value & Vehicle Odometer Gauge
ch01.description: Visual representation of 5-digit number place value columns (TTh, Th, H, T, O) and odometer distance delta calculation.

ch02.title: Fraction Strip Kit & Equal Partition Model
ch02.description: Visual fraction kit demonstrating 1 Whole, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 strips and equivalent fraction alignment.

ch03.title: Clock Radial Angles & Rotational Geometry
ch03.description: Clock face radial angles showing 30-degree hourly divisions, right angles (90°), acute, obtuse, and straight angles.

ch04.title: 5-Digit Column Regrouping & Palindrome Cascade
ch04.description: Column addition/subtraction with regrouping across zero and 4-step reverse-and-add palindrome generation.

ch05.title: Metric Length Hierarchy & Double Number Line
ch05.description: Double number line showing proportional metric conversions between mm, cm, m, and km.

ch06.title: 2x2 Partial Product Grid Area Model
ch06.description: Distributive property 2x2 partial product grid decomposing multi-digit multiplication.

ch07.title: Surface Tessellations & Unfolded 3D Polyhedron Nets
ch07.description: Seamless tiling tessellation vertex angle rules (360°) and unfolded 6-face cube net with Euler formula F+V-E=2.

ch08.title: Pan Balance Equilibrium & Mass/Capacity Scale
ch08.description: Pan balance equilibrium with target mass, counterweights, and quintal/tonne conversion scale.

ch09.title: Partial Quotient Chunking & Division Identity Matrix
ch09.description: Partial quotient division algorithm chunking multiples and verifying Dividend = Divisor x Quotient + Remainder.

ch10.title: Reflection Lines & Rotational Firki Pinwheel
ch10.description: Mirror reflection axes of symmetry and 4-blade firki pinwheel with 1/4 turn (90°) rotational order.

ch11.title: 1D Perimeter Boundary vs 2D Enclosed Surface Area
ch11.description: Comparison of 1D outer boundary perimeter (16 cm) and 2D enclosed grid surface area (15 sq cm).

ch12.title: Base-60 Time System & Athletic Digital Stopwatch
ch12.description: Digital stopwatch with split seconds and 12-hour AM/PM to 24-hour railway clock translation.

ch13.title: Animal Jump Number Line & Factor Tile Arrays
ch13.description: Mowgli (2-unit) and Robby (3-unit) jump paths on a number line locating shared LCM spot at 6.

ch14.title: Cartesian Grid Coordinates & Navigation Map
ch14.description: Cartesian coordinate grid system with origin (0,0), X-axis, Y-axis, and plotted coordinate points (x, y).

ch15.title: 5-Line Tally Bundles & Scaled Frequency Bar Graph
ch15.description: Data collection using 5-line tally mark bundles (卌) and scaled frequency bar graph analytics.
